baseline_prompt_en: An observational photograph of fictional Korean marines enacting military black comedy: a pompous ceremonial response to a trivial mishap. A faded olive minibus has stopped on a sunlit coastal road, its near rear tire visibly squashed against the asphalt; a small unattached spare wheel stands upright a few steps in front of it, waiting to be fitted. The central woman uses the supplied portrait as a face-and-hair appearance guide, retaining its soft oval face, dark eyes, short dark cheek-length bob and lightly separated fringe. In a plain red marine training shirt, loose camouflage trousers and dusty boots, she stands to the left of the spare wheel and grips one wooden ceremonial flagpole with both hands, her forearms visibly joining the grip. Its broad red fabric hangs from a crossbar and projects a distinct patch of shade across the spare wheel. Her nearly level face turns toward the other marine with a tiny suppressed smile, the sunlight catching the unforced warmth of her eyes. To the right, a separate stocky marine stands rigidly at attention and gives the spare wheel a solemn hand salute; his face and torso turn down toward that wheel as if this ordinary repair deserved a parade. The wheel, the flag shade, both connected grips and the saluting figure read together across the foreground. The minibus, the road continuing toward the sea, and a small open toolbox establish an interrupted journey. A medium-wide, eye-level view keeps her face legible and the vehicle failure visible, with bright dry daylight, tactile roadside dust and a deadpan road-movie stillness.
